name: İskenderun
title: İskenderun Thickness Measurement | Steel Port Bulk Carrier UTM
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at İskenderun: holds, hoppers, hatch covers and ballast tanks on Capesizes and bulk carriers at the steel and bulk terminals.
h1: Ship Thickness Gauging in İskenderun Bay: Steelworks, Bulk Terminals and Anchorages
intro: İskenderun, at the head of the gulf that bears its name in Turkey's far eastern Mediterranean corner, is a steel and bulk port. Capesizes and Panamaxes bring iron ore and coal to the integrated and electric-arc steelworks along the bay, steel products and project cargo leave from private terminals, and container ships use the rebuilt city port. Long discharges and waits in the sheltered bay make good gauging windows. Each job is staffed from India, with the team travelling out once the agent confirms the ship's line-up.

highlights.h: Ore and coal discharges at the steelworks
highlights.p: İsdemir's port takes bulk carriers of up to about 200,000 tonnes, and other steelmakers' terminals around the bay take Capesizes too. Grab discharge over several days opens holds one at a time for tank top, hopper and frame measurement.

The gulf is enclosed by coast and mountains on three sides, and ships waiting for steelworks berths can lie at anchor for some time. That wait can be used for ballast tank and empty-hold gauging, reached by launch, while cargo is not competing for the crew's attention.

The February 2023 earthquakes and the fire that followed badly damaged İskenderun's container port. Its quays reopened in stages through 2023 and repairs continued afterwards, so container ships once again call at the city port on regional services.

p: İskenderun lies on the eastern shore of the Gulf of İskenderun, the deep inlet that cuts into Turkey's south coast between the Çukurova plain and the Amanos mountains, not far from the Syrian border. The gulf is broad, with the city port and the steelworks on its eastern and north-eastern shores and the Ceyhan oil terminals and Yumurtalık on the opposite side, so a single bay holds several independent ports. Approaches from the open Mediterranean involve no locks, bars or significant tides, and the shape of the gulf gives ships at anchor shelter from most directions. Pilotage and towage are provided at each terminal, and berth allocation at the private steel jetties follows each plant's own production schedule rather than a common port plan.

Steel defines the traffic. İsdemir, part of the Oyak group's Erdemir business, runs an integrated works at Payas with its own port handling bulk, general and project cargo, and a chain of private terminals along the bay serves electric-arc steelmakers, ore and coal importers and steel exporters, among them Tosyalı's facilities and the bulk terminals at Sarıseki. Iron ore, coal and scrap come in, mostly in Capesize, Panamax and Supramax bulk carriers, while finished and semi-finished steel goes out in general cargo and multipurpose ships. Fertiliser and grain handlers add further bulk traffic, and the bay also has liquid terminals and an LNG floating storage and regasification unit at Dörtyol on its eastern shore. The result is a bay where most ships arrive to discharge raw materials and leave in ballast.

The city port tells a different story. Limak's container and multipurpose port at İskenderun was badly damaged in the February 2023 earthquakes, when a fire in the container stacks took days to bring under control, and its quays reopened in stages in April, May and October of that year as repair work went on. Container ships on Mediterranean and Middle East services call there again, and the operator has said it aims to restore and then exceed its former capacity. For ship inspection, though, İskenderun is mostly about the dry bulk and steel trades, and with heavy ship repair concentrated far away in the Marmara, the information gathered here usually feeds a docking that will be planned and carried out somewhere else.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens around İskenderun Bay
p: At the steelworks and bulk terminals, gauging follows discharge. Grab unloaders work the holds in turn, and as each is emptied and cleaned we measure tank top, hopper slopes, lower stools, frames and brackets, the areas that take the punishment from ore, coal and scrap. Hatch covers and coamings can be measured while the covers are open, and ballast tanks once the ship is ballasting for departure. Steel export berths offer similar access on general cargo and multipurpose ships, usually before loading starts, when holds are empty and dry. Every terminal runs its own access and safety rules, which the ship's agent clears before the team arrives.

At anchor, a ship waiting for a steelworks berth can be gauged by launch, and because the gulf is sheltered the work is less weather-dependent than on an open coast. Container ships at the Limak port give short, scheduled windows suited to deck structure and scrubber piping. Docking is another matter: there is no large repair yard in the bay, so ships that need steel renewal sail to Tuzla, Yalova or yards abroad, taking the İskenderun readings with them as the basis for the yard's steel estimate.
list: İsdemir port at Payas — hold, hopper and inner bottom gauging on large bulk carriers discharging iron ore and coal for the integrated works.
Private steel and bulk terminals along the bay — ore, coal and scrap carriers measured as holds are discharged, within each terminal's rules.
Steel export berths — general cargo and multipurpose ships gauged in empty holds and on hatch covers before loading.
Limak İskenderun port — deck, coaming and scrubber piping checks on container ships during scheduled calls.
İskenderun Bay anchorages — ballast tank and empty-hold gauging on ships waiting for steelworks berths, reached by launch.
Ceyhan and Yumurtalık terminals across the gulf — follow-on tanker and bulk work within the same mobilisation.

context.h: Port state control and the steel trade in the eastern Mediterranean
p: Turkey belongs to the Mediterranean MoU and the Black Sea MoU, and the ships serving İskenderun's steel industry include a large share of older bulk carriers and general cargo ships, many trading between the eastern Mediterranean, the Black Sea and the Middle East. Inspectors look hard at hatch covers, coamings and hold structure on these ships, along with air pipes, ventilators and ballast tank condition, and structural deficiencies are a familiar cause of delay in this sector. Gauging the doubtful items before the ship returns to the bay is usually simpler than dealing with repairs ordered at a port state control inspection.

The trade itself shapes the inspection need. Ore and coal arrive on long hauls from several continents as well as on shorter routes from the Black Sea, so the Capesizes and Panamaxes at İskenderun are typical mid-life ships of the global bulk fleet, while the scrap and steel trades use smaller, older ships on short regional voyages with little time in port. Steel exporters fixing ships for coil, rebar and plate also look for hatch covers that keep cargo dry, so cover condition is a commercial question as much as a survey item. Ships trading on to EU ports carry EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime obligations for those voyages and need an Inventory of Hazardous Materials.

psc: Black Sea MoU and Mediterranean MoU

jobs.p: Most İskenderun work comes from the bulk and steel trades. Superintendents of Capesizes and Panamaxes use discharges at the steelworks to measure holds and ballast tanks before a renewal or intermediate survey; owners of scrap and general cargo ships want hatch covers, coamings and holds checked between cargoes; buyers ask for condition surveys on ships waiting at anchor; and container lines book scrubber piping checks at the city port. Because the nearest docking yards are far away, many programmes end as a pre-docking estimate sent to a Marmara or overseas yard. Each one is planned around the terminal's own berthing programme.
list: Hold, hopper and transverse bulkhead gauging on a Capesize after iron ore discharge at İsdemir, ahead of its fourth renewal survey.
Hatch cover and coaming gauging on a general cargo ship before loading coil at a steel export berth, after leaks damaged a previous cargo.
Ballast tank gauging on a Panamax waiting at anchor in the bay for a coal berth, giving the superintendent corrosion data before docking.
Pre-purchase gauging of a Supramax in the scrap trade at anchor off İskenderun, with holds and hatch covers included for the buyer.
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping checks on a container ship during a call at the Limak port.

logistics: Çukurova International Airport near Tarsus, usually reached through Istanbul, is the normal gateway, followed by a drive east around the gulf; Hatay Airport, between İskenderun and Antakya, may also be an option depending on current schedules. Terminal access at the steelworks and private bulk terminals, ISPS passes at the city port and launches for anchorage boarding are all arranged through the ship's agent. Each technician from India needs a Turkish visa, so we start applications when a likely call is identified and plan around berth line-ups that shift with the steelworks' needs.

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged during iron ore discharge at the İskenderun steelworks?
faqs.a: Yes, hold by hold. Once a hold is discharged, swept and released by the chief officer, we measure the tank top, hopper slopes, stools and frames, focusing on grab damage and areas with a corrosion history. Ballast tanks follow when the ship ballasts for departure. Each steelworks terminal has its own access and safety rules, which the agent clears before the team boards.

faqs.q: Is the anchorage in İskenderun Bay suitable for gauging?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. The gulf is sheltered, and ships waiting for steelworks berths often lie at anchor long enough for a ballast tank programme or measurement of empty holds. A launch is booked through the agent. Work at anchor still depends on the master's agreement and on spaces being ventilated and certified, and the plan allows for the ship being called to berth earlier than expected.

faqs.q: Where do ships calling at İskenderun go for steel renewal?
faqs.a: Usually to the Marmara yards at Tuzla and Yalova, or to yards outside Turkey, because there is no ocean-going repair yard in the bay. That makes a measured steel estimate from İskenderun valuable: the yard can plan plate and labour before the ship sails, and the readings can be checked again at the same points in dock.

faqs.q: Has the 2023 earthquake affected port access at İskenderun?
faqs.a: The container port operated by Limak was hit hardest, with quay damage and a major fire, and its berths reopened in stages during 2023 while repairs continued. The steelworks and private bulk terminals along the bay each have their own operating status. The ship's agent is the best source on current berth availability, and we plan each job around the terminal the ship is actually using.
